questions: How should the CLI extract headings from HTML reports while maintaining backward compatibility with Markdown reports?
Should the CLI add an HTML parsing dependency?

answers.answer: Use dual regex patterns: try HTML heading pattern first, then fall back to existing Markdown heading regex. HTML pattern: /<h([1-6])(?:\s+[^>]*?id="([^"]*)"[^>]*)?>(.+?)<\/h\1>/i captures level, id attribute, and text. For comment anchor lookup, use the id attribute if present, otherwise slugify the text (with HTML tags stripped). Display format is identical to Markdown: '## Title [slug] (N comments: ...)'.

answers.answer: No. The CLI has zero runtime dependencies by design. A regex pattern is sufficient for the narrow task of extracting h1-h6 heading elements from well-formed HTML. Adding cheerio or node-html-parser would be over-engineered for this single use case.

statement: CLI changes are minimal: add an HTML heading regex pattern alongside the existing Markdown regex in show.ts for dual-format heading extraction. Add filePath to the local type for format detection. No new dependencies needed, preserving the zero-dep design.
